summary: Nora tidies her own notebook: notes about the same occasion are merged, and questions that have been answered or overtaken are retired.
details: Two notes about the same date and the same people are combined into one that keeps everything both of them said, including any disagreement.
A note whose occasion has passed, or whose question somebody has actually answered, stops appearing.
limitations: Merging is decided by the date and people a note is anchored to, never by how similar two notes read — two weddings stay two notes.
Nothing is merged or retired until the background loop is switched on for a room.
